historical_references.reference: Sarvan, also known as Sarvanabhava or Sarvanamuktananda, was a 15th-century Jain monk and philosopher. He is known for his work 'Tattvartha-sutra-bindu', a commentary on the Tattvartha-sutra, the fundamental text of Jain philosophy. The work is significant for its comprehensive discussion on various aspects of Jain philosophy.

Sarvan, a prominent Hindu king of the Satavahana dynasty, ruled during the 2nd century AD. He is known for his patronage of Buddhism and Jainism, and his coins bear inscriptions in both Prakrit and Greek, reflecting his multicultural kingdom.
